title: Shotguns and his father's quail hunting
summary: Guns, and his father hunting quail from horseback with trained dogs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What kind of shotgun is it? Just said again. That's a Remington.
Oh, that's not bad. No, sir. It's one of the best.
I had a Parker double barrel.
Parker was a fine gun. Yeah. My daddy loved a Parker. But my father was one of the finest quail shots in North Mississippi. But his favorite was Ithaca.
I don't think I ever shot a Ithaca in my life.
Ithaca was a lightweight gun. My father hunted quail off horseback. He had two very fine bird dogs. One was a Llewellyn setter. The other one was an English pointer. And he never got off his horse.
That must have been a good horse to stand still for all that.
The dogs would point and they'd flush and he'd kill two quail all the time. And the dogs were trained to go and retrieve and they would ray up on the side of the horse and hand him the birds.
I got the write up about him. Riddick the Crackshot.
